'''Luis Fernando de la Peña Auerbach'''{{Family name footnote|[[de la Peña]]|[[Auerbach (surname)|Auerbach]]|lang=Mexican}} (23 July 1931 – 17 May 2026), known as '''Luis de la Peña''', was a Mexican physicist. He was a researcher of the Institute of Physics and professor of the Faculty of Sciences of the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM) and was a member of the Science Advisory Council of the Presidency of Mexico.

==Life and career==
De la Peña was born in [[San Martín Texmelucan]], Puebla, in 1931.<ref name=jornada/> He graduated from ESIME of the [[National Polytechnic Institute]] (IPN) with a degree in mechanical-electrical engineering and began his professional activity as a designer of audio systems. From 1954 was professor of the ESIME and from 1958 definitively joined UNAM. He completed his PhD in 1964 under the direction of [[Arseny Sokolov]] at [[Moscow State University]] in the [[Soviet Union]].{{sfn|Jammer|1974|p=433}}

He is known most for his contributions towards the field of [[stochastic electrodynamics]] (SED). In 2002 he was awarded the [[National Prize for Arts and Sciences]] in the Physics, Mathematics, and Natural Sciences category.<ref>{{cite web | title=Lista oficial de ganadores de los Premios Nacionales 2002 | website=La Jornada | date=November 15, 2002 | url=https://web.jornada.com.mx/2002/11/15/05an2cul.php | language=es | access-date=September 8, 2026}}</ref>

De la Peña died in [[Mexico City]] on 17 May 2026, at the age of 94.<ref name=jornada>{{cite news |title=Murió el físico Luis de la Peña Auerbach |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/2026/05/19/ciencias/a06n3cie |access-date=21 May 2026 |work=[[La Jornada]] |date=19 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Gutiérrez Alcalá |first1=Roberto |title="Luis de la Peña dejó un gran hueco, pero llenó muchos": Ana María Cetto |url=https://www.gaceta.unam.mx/luis-de-la-pena-dejo-un-gran-hueco-pero-lleno-muchos-ana-maria-cetto/ |work=Gaceta |agency=[[Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México]] |date=21 May 2026}}</ref>
